body:
Today's scan came back empty — zero arbitrage opportunities across the 89 live contracts checked on Kalshi and Polymarket. That's a legitimate, unremarkable finding: prices on both venues are internally consistent with no mispriced overlap large enough (after fees) to clear the scanner's threshold.

The strike ladder itself looks unusual if you're used to gold trading near $2,000-$2,600, but it lines up with where the metal actually is right now. As of 8:26 a.m. ET, gold was trading around $4,445.96 per ounce, and the all-time high was $5,597.23, set on January 29, 2026. Gold shot through the $3,500 mark and moved from $3,500 to $4,000 in just 36 days in October 2025, so today's clustering of Kalshi strikes between $4,050 and $4,800 and Polymarket's touch-levels around $4,000-$4,400 both reflect the same extraordinary run rather than a pricing anomaly on either platform.

Worth flagging for anyone eyeballing the raw tables: Kalshi's contracts here are settlement bets tied to a fixed date (September 30 or December 31, 2026, at spot), while Polymarket's are "touch" contracts asking whether gold dips to a given low at any point during the month — a different question with a different resolution rule, so an apparent price gap between similar-looking strikes on the two platforms isn't automatically capturable. Several Kalshi strikes also show 24-hour volume of zero, meaning quoted bid-ask spreads there are stale rather than tradeable. Nothing today points to a genuine cross-platform edge; it's a quiet, structurally normal day.
headline: Zero arbitrage found across 89 gold contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket
